rules: 113.7a Once activated or triggered, an ability exists on the stack independently of its source. Destruction or removal of the source after that time won’t affect the ability. Note that some abilities cause a source to do something (for example, “This creature deals 1 damage to any target”) rather than the ability doing anything directly. In these cases, any activated or triggered ability that references information about the source for use while announcing an activated ability or putting a triggered ability on the stack checks that information when the ability is put onto the stack. Otherwise, it will check that information when it resolves. In both instances, if the source is no longer in the zone it’s expected to be in at that time, its last known information is used. The source can still perform the action even though it no longer exists.
723.3. Only control of the player changes. All objects are controlled by their normal controllers. A player who’s being controlled during their turn is still the active player.

723.5. While controlling another player, a player makes all choices and decisions the controlled player is allowed to make or is told to make by the rules or by any objects. This includes choices and decisions about what to play, and choices and decisions called for by spells and abilities.
723.5a The controller of another player can use only that player’s resources (cards, mana, and so on) to pay costs for that player.
723.6. The controller of another player can’t make that player concede. A player may concede the game at any time, even if they are controlled by another player. See rule 104.3a.
723.9. An effect may give a player control of themselves. That player will make their own decisions and choices as normal.

Actor ownership, opponents and payment resources are unchanged. Beneficiary follows current native controller links and remains fixed during a rollout even after control ends or its master loses.

Chain and self contexts additionally use native controller APIs, not a claim of complete card-generated control chains. Cyclic or cross-game contexts are rejected explicitly; full custom/human agent semantics remain unverified.

Sixteen packaged cases observe actual legal choices, costs, canonical pending spell/ability targets, original-world independence while planning and native outcomes. Selected sacrificed-source activated abilities are checked, not every trigger or stack policy.

Both requested heuristic/full modes are exercised. Controlled heuristic actions route through legal-action planning; ordinary heuristic behavior is retained and the ordinary damage-counter positive explicitly uses unchanged shipped Cautious policy.
Primary heuristic ControlPlayer support remains open. Full-mode candidate admission for three legal affordable actions does not establish useful future-turn evaluation or selection.
Combat/blocks, mandatory choices, search-only control, arbitrary response priority, stochastic future effects, hidden/merged/perpetual state and suspended continuations require separate validation.

Unmapped callback diagnostics are asserted in fixtures, not yet aggregated into regular CLI reports. Catalog construction and versioned rules references do not establish complete or current rules compliance.
